strengths: Learning LLVM representations from aligned source code and comments addresses a relevant problem with an identifiable audience in machine learning for program analysis. Using these additional modalities during pretraining while retaining an encoder for binary inputs is a useful design. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-02q49wa0/call-3305b245539b44c49c1a813d8c947947/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The reported results are promising: function-name accuracy increases from 29.41 to 33.41 over RoBERTa, and summarization BLEU-4 increases from 32.43 to 34.36 over GraphCodeBERT. Evaluating four downstream tasks provides useful breadth.

The manuscript includes component ablations, a comparison of comment sources, and a CodeT5 extension. The high-level workflow is understandable, and the stated release of data, code, and configurations provides a useful foundation for replication.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the evaluation protocol inconsistencies. Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 POJ classes, but Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint training, validation, and test labels. Under ordinary classification, the test classes receive no positive training examples. If this is actually retrieval, specify the training objective, candidate pools, and MAP/MAR/MAF1 definitions. This affects the main results and ablations. Also reconcile Section 3.2's statement that generation is evaluated on validation data with Section 4.3's test-set description, and document the pretraining/downstream partitions.

Necessary: Match the binary-analysis claims to the evaluated inputs. The experiments use compiler-emitted LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function and type names. This differs materially from analyzing stripped executable binaries; the assertion that these representations are trivially interchangeable is incorrect. Narrow the conclusions to the evaluated LLVM setting, or provide evidence using representations recovered from stripped executables.

Necessary: The ablations do not isolate the contribution of interpolation. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70, and the stages also change the contrastive objective. Section 5.1 asserts convergence without supporting measurements. Comparable training-budget and objective controls are needed to attribute gains specifically to interpolation; separate scalar and feature-wise mixing controls would support claims about their individual benefits.

Necessary: The conclusions about human-written comments exceed the evidence. Table 7 reports MAF1 of 3.06 with human comments, 37.40 without comments, and 38.19 with generated comments. This striking collapse deserves investigation, but comment extraction, matched program coverage, length handling, and variability across runs are insufficiently documented. Length distributions alone do not establish the proposed causal explanations involving verbosity and style. Supply controlled evidence or restrict the finding to this corpus and configuration.

Necessary: Lexical generation metrics and selected examples do not establish semantic correctness or human comprehension. As printed, Figure 8 contains 'do_exit_group(status << );' in both the reference and ContraBin output, which is syntactically incomplete. Audit whether this reflects figure preparation or target preprocessing. Clarify the provenance of summarization references and provide functional or human evaluation if retaining the semantic-consistency claims; otherwise describe the results as reference-text reconstruction.

Necessary: Make the implemented learning rule unambiguous. Equations 8 and 10 feed H1 + H2 into the interpolation network, whereas Figure 3 depicts concatenation. Section 2.2 discusses source/binary interpolation, while Section 2.4 describes source/comment interpolation, and Algorithm 1 permits arbitrary pairs. These choices change gradient flow and the learned objective. Reconcile them and specify the actual interpolation dimensions, checkpoint initialization, and temperature.

Necessary: Calibrate the comparative conclusions. Table 6 gives ContraBin lower BLEU-4 than GraphCodeBERT, 71.14 versus 71.56, while exact match improves only from 24.73 to 25.16. Without uncertainty estimates, these results do not establish considerable improvements across all four tasks. Narrow the superiority claims or substantiate the small differences. Also correct Section 5.1's confusion between relative percentages and percentage-point ablation drops.

Optional: Shorten the repeated human-learning analogies and expand comparisons with binary/IR-specific representation models. These would improve presentation and context; the recommendation primarily reflects unresolved evidence and protocol issues, rather than a requirement for greater novelty or state-of-the-art performance.
